senses.def: used before a singular countable noun when it is not a specific one or has not been mentioned before
examples: I saw a fox in the backyard this morning.
She works as a nurse at a hospital downtown.

senses.def: used to mean 'each' or 'per' with amounts, prices and frequencies
examples: The gym costs forty dollars a month.
I drink coffee three times a day.

note: Use "an" before a vowel sound: an hour, an idea, but a university, a one-way street.

senses.def: the skill, power or opportunity to do something
examples: She has the ability to stay calm under pressure.
The disease affects a patient's ability to walk.

collocations: to the best of your ability

senses.def: having the skill, chance or power to do something; used in "be able to"
examples: Will you be able to come to the meeting tomorrow?
After the surgery, he was able to walk again.

senses.def: clever or good at doing something
examples: She is one of the most able students in her class.

note: "Can" has no future or perfect forms, so use "be able to": I will be able to, I have been able to.

senses.def: to officially end a law, system or institution
examples: Many countries have abolished the death penalty.
The new government promised to abolish the tax on books.

senses.def: a medical procedure that deliberately ends a pregnancy at an early stage
examples: The state passed a law restricting access to abortion.
Abortion remains one of the most divisive issues in American politics.

note: A natural loss of a pregnancy is a "miscarriage" (düşük), not an abortion. "Abort" also means to stop a plan or process.

senses.def: on the subject of or connected with someone or something
examples: We talked about our plans for the summer.
What's the book about?

senses.def: a little more or less than a number or time
examples: The flight takes about three hours.
There were about fifty people at the party.

senses.def: used in "be about to" to say something will happen very soon
examples: I was just about to call you when you walked in.

senses.def: in or to a higher position than something
examples: There's a small shelf above the sink.
The plane flew high above the clouds.

senses.def: more than a particular number, amount or level
examples: Temperatures rose above 100 degrees last week.
The tour is for children aged ten and above.

senses.def: at or to a higher place, or earlier in a piece of writing
examples: The neighbors in the apartment above are very noisy.
Please contact us at the address given above.

note: "Above all" means "most importantly". "Above" is for position/level; "over" can also mean covering or moving across.

senses.def: in or to a foreign country
examples: She spent a year studying abroad in Spain.
More Americans are traveling abroad than ever before.

note: An adverb, so no preposition: "go abroad", not "go to abroad". But you can say "from abroad".

senses.def: the fact of being away from a place where you are expected, or the period you are away
examples: Her frequent absences from work worried her manager.
He returned to the team after a two-month absence.

senses.def: the fact that something does not exist or is missing
examples: In the absence of evidence, the police had to release him.
The absence of clear rules caused confusion.

senses.def: not present in a place where you are expected to be, for example because of illness
examples: Three students were absent from class today with the flu.
He was absent from the meeting without explanation.

senses.def: not existing in a place or situation where you would expect it
examples: Any sense of humor was completely absent from his speech.

senses.def: total and complete; used to emphasize something
examples: The trip was an absolute disaster from start to finish.
I have absolute confidence in her judgment.

senses.def: having unlimited power, or not depending on or compared with anything else
examples: The king held absolute power over the country.
Measured in absolute terms, wages have risen.

senses.def: completely or totally; used to emphasize what you are saying
examples: The view from the top was absolutely amazing.
I have absolutely no idea where my keys are.

senses.def: used as a strong way of saying yes or agreeing
examples: "Can I bring a friend?" "Absolutely!"
"Absolutely not," she said when he asked to borrow her car.

note: Use with extreme adjectives (absolutely freezing, absolutely delicious), not usually with gradable ones (not "absolutely cold").

senses.def: to take in a liquid, gas, heat or other substance
examples: The towel absorbed most of the spilled milk.
Dark clothes absorb more heat from the sun.

senses.def: to take in and understand information fully
examples: There was too much information to absorb in one lecture.

senses.def: to hold someone's attention completely
examples: He was so absorbed in his game that he didn't hear me.

senses.def: based on general ideas rather than real, physical things or specific situations
examples: Justice and freedom are abstract concepts.
The discussion was too abstract for most of the students.

senses.def: (of art) using shapes and colors rather than showing people or things realistically
examples: The museum has a large collection of abstract paintings.

senses.def: a short summary of a research article or academic paper
examples: Read the abstract first to see if the study is relevant.

note: Opposite: concrete (somut).

senses.def: completely unreasonable or silly, and not making sense
examples: It's absurd to charge ten dollars for a bottle of water.
The idea sounded absurd at first, but it worked.

senses.def: a very large amount of something, more than is needed
examples: The region has an abundance of fresh water.
Wild berries grow in abundance along the trail.

note: Formal. "In abundance" comes after the noun: "Food was available in abundance."

senses.def: the wrong or harmful use of something, such as power or drugs
examples: The scandal involved a clear abuse of power.
He spent years struggling with drug abuse.

senses.def: cruel or violent treatment of a person or animal
examples: The charity supports victims of child abuse.
She reported the abuse to the police.

senses.def: to use something wrongly or too much, in a way that causes harm
examples: The officer was accused of abusing his authority.
Some people abuse prescription painkillers.

senses.def: to treat a person or animal cruelly or violently
examples: The dog had been abused by its previous owner.

note: Pronunciation differs: noun /əˈbjuːs/ (s sound), verb /əˈbjuːz/ (z sound).

senses.def: connected with education, especially study and research at schools and universities
examples: The new academic year starts in late August.
Her academic performance improved after she joined the study group.

senses.def: a person who teaches or does research at a university or college
examples: The report was written by a group of leading academics.

senses.def: not relevant to a real situation; only of theoretical interest
examples: The question is purely academic now that the decision has been made.

senses.def: a school or college that gives training in a special skill or subject
examples: He graduated from the police academy last spring.
She trained at a famous ballet academy in New York.

senses.def: an official organization of respected scholars, scientists or artists
examples: She was elected to the National Academy of Sciences.

senses.def: to happen or make something happen faster or earlier
examples: The government wants to accelerate the switch to clean energy.
Climate change has accelerated the melting of glaciers.

senses.def: (of a vehicle or driver) to go faster
examples: The car accelerated as it merged onto the highway.

note: Opposite: decelerate / slow down. The car pedal is the "accelerator" or informally the "gas pedal".

senses.def: a way of pronouncing a language that shows where someone comes from
examples: She speaks English with a slight French accent.
I could tell from his accent that he grew up in Texas.

senses.def: special emphasis given to a syllable, or a particular focus on something
examples: In "hotel", the accent is on the second syllable.
The menu puts the accent on local ingredients.

senses.def: to take something that is offered or say yes to an offer or invitation
examples: She accepted the job offer without hesitation.
Do you accept credit cards?

senses.def: to agree that something is true or to deal with a difficult situation without trying to change it
examples: He finally accepted that the relationship was over.
You have to accept some risk when you invest.

senses.def: to allow someone to join a group, school or organization
examples: She was accepted to three different colleges.

note: Don't confuse with "except" (hariç). Turkish "kabul etmek" also translates as "admit" when confessing something.

senses.def: agreed or approved of by most people in a society
examples: Smoking indoors is no longer socially acceptable.
Violence is never an acceptable way to solve problems.

senses.def: good enough, but not excellent
examples: The hotel was clean and the price was acceptable.

senses.def: the act of saying yes to an offer, invitation or gift
examples: She gave an emotional acceptance speech at the awards ceremony.
Please confirm your acceptance of the offer by Friday.

senses.def: the fact of being approved of or welcomed, or of agreeing that something difficult is true
examples: The theory gained wide acceptance among scientists.
Grief eventually gave way to acceptance.

senses.def: the right, opportunity or way to use, reach or enter something
examples: Many rural areas still lack access to fast internet.
Students have free access to the library's databases.

senses.def: to open or use a computer file, system or information
examples: You can access your account from any device.
Hackers accessed the personal data of thousands of customers.

note: Noun takes "to": access to clean water. The verb takes no preposition: access the files (not "access to the files").

senses.def: possible to reach, enter or use, including for people with disabilities
examples: The island is only accessible by boat.
All the station's entrances are wheelchair accessible.

senses.def: easy to understand or enjoy
examples: The book makes complex science accessible to ordinary readers.

senses.def: an unexpected event, often involving a vehicle, that causes damage or injury
examples: He broke his leg in a car accident last year.
Most accidents happen close to home.

senses.def: something that happens by chance, without being planned
examples: I found the old photos by accident while cleaning the attic.
It was no accident that she got the job.

senses.def: by chance or by mistake, without intending to
examples: I accidentally deleted the whole folder.
She accidentally locked herself out of the house.

note: Opposite: deliberately / on purpose. "Accidentally on purpose" is a joke meaning secretly on purpose.

senses.def: to provide a place to stay or have enough space for a number of people or things
examples: The hotel can accommodate up to 300 guests.
The new stadium accommodates 60,000 fans.

senses.def: to consider and try to meet someone's needs or wishes
examples: The airline did its best to accommodate passengers with special needs.
We can adjust the schedule to accommodate your request.

note: Common spelling mistake: double c and double m — accommodate.

senses.def: a place to stay, live or work in; in American English usually "accommodations"
examples: The price includes flights and hotel accommodations.
Finding cheap accommodation near campus is difficult.

senses.def: a change or arrangement that helps someone, especially a person with a disability
examples: Students with dyslexia may receive accommodations such as extra time on tests.

note: In American English, the plural "accommodations" is usual for lodging; British English uses the uncountable "accommodation".

senses.def: to go somewhere with someone
examples: Children under 12 must be accompanied by an adult.
She accompanied her father to his doctor's appointment.

senses.def: to happen or exist together with something else
examples: The fever was accompanied by a bad headache.
Each photo is accompanied by a short description.

senses.def: to play music while someone sings or plays the main part
examples: She sang while her brother accompanied her on the piano.

note: No preposition after it: "accompany someone", not "accompany with someone".

senses.def: to succeed in doing or finishing something, especially after effort
examples: We accomplished a lot in our first week.
The team accomplished its goal of raising $10,000.

senses.def: an impressive thing that someone achieves after a lot of work
examples: Finishing the marathon was a huge accomplishment for her.
The report lists the company's main accomplishments this year.

senses.def: the act of successfully completing something
examples: The accomplishment of the mission took three years.

senses.tr: (in accordance with) uyarınca, -e uygun olarak, -e göre
senses.def: used in "in accordance with" to mean following a rule, law or someone's wishes
examples: The funds were spent in accordance with the law.
His body was cremated in accordance with his wishes.

note: Formal; almost always used in the phrase "in accordance with".

senses.def: as stated or reported by someone or something
examples: According to the weather forecast, it will rain tomorrow.
According to police, the driver was not injured.

senses.def: following or depending on a plan, rule or system
examples: Everything went according to plan.
Students are grouped according to their ability.

note: Don't say "according to me" for your own opinion; say "in my opinion" or "I think".

senses.tr: buna göre, ona göre, uygun şekilde
senses.def: in a way that suits what has been said or what is happening
examples: The weather can change quickly, so dress accordingly.
We'll find out how many people are coming and plan accordingly.

senses.def: for that reason; as a result
examples: The company lost its biggest client. Accordingly, it had to cut jobs.

senses.def: an arrangement with a bank or online service to keep money or use the service
examples: I opened a savings account at my local bank.
You need to create an account to leave a comment.

senses.def: a spoken or written description of an event
examples: Witnesses gave different accounts of the accident.
By all accounts, the concert was a success.

senses.def: used in "account for" to mean explain something or form a particular amount of a total
examples: How do you account for the missing money?
Women account for 60% of the workforce.

note: "Take something into account" = hesaba katmak. "On account of" = because of (formal).

senses.def: the fact of being responsible for your decisions and actions and having to explain them
examples: Voters are demanding greater accountability from elected officials.
There was no accountability for the mistakes that were made.

senses.def: responsible for your decisions or actions and expected to explain them
examples: Police officers must be held accountable for their actions.
Managers are accountable to the board of directors.

note: Accountable to a person or group; accountable for an action or result.

senses.def: a person whose job is to keep or check financial records
examples: Our accountant helps us file our taxes every April.
She works as an accountant for a large firm.

note: In the US, a qualified accountant is a CPA (certified public accountant).

senses.def: to gradually collect or get more and more of something over time
examples: He accumulated a huge collection of vinyl records.
Over the years, she accumulated a lot of debt.

senses.def: to gradually increase in amount
examples: Dust had accumulated on the old bookshelves.
Snow accumulated quickly overnight.

senses.def: the gradual increase of something, or an amount that has built up over time
examples: The accumulation of fat in the arteries can lead to heart disease.
There was a large accumulation of snow on the roof.

senses.def: the quality of being exact and correct, or the ability to do something without mistakes
examples: Journalists must check the accuracy of their sources.
The new test detects the disease with 95% accuracy.

senses.def: correct and exact in every detail
examples: The weather forecast was surprisingly accurate.
We need an accurate count of how many people are coming.

senses.def: in a way that is correct and exact
examples: It's hard to accurately predict the stock market.
The movie accurately portrays life in the 1950s.

senses.def: a statement saying that someone has done something wrong or illegal
examples: He denied all accusations of cheating.
The senator faces accusations of corruption.

senses.def: to say that someone has done something wrong or illegal
examples: She accused her coworker of stealing her ideas.
He was accused of murder but found not guilty.

note: Pattern: accuse someone OF doing something (not "for"). Compare: blame someone FOR something.

senses.def: the person or people on trial for a crime
examples: The accused was led into the courtroom in handcuffs.
The jury found the accused not guilty.

note: Always used with "the": "the accused" can be singular or plural, with no -s.

senses.def: to succeed in reaching a goal or standard, especially after a lot of effort
examples: She worked hard to achieve her dream of becoming a doctor.
The country achieved independence in 1960.

senses.def: something you have done successfully, especially through effort and skill
examples: Winning the championship was the greatest achievement of his career.
The report celebrates the achievements of local volunteers.

senses.def: the act or process of reaching a goal or standard
examples: The program aims to raise academic achievement in poor neighborhoods.
